terms.gloss: I am going to do, I am about to do
terms.grammar: the future participle, agreeing with the subject, with sum
evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.32: quid agis, quid āctūrus es?
Aug. Conf. 11.28.38: dictūrus sum canticum quod nōvī
terms.comment: What someone means to do or is on the point of doing; in the past, factūrus eram, I was going to. The plain future says only that it will happen (see will).

terms.gloss: it is just about to happen
terms.grammar: impersonal phrase, with ut and the subjunctive
evidence: Liv. 2.17.5: cum jam in eō esset, ut in mūrōs ēvāderet mīles (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a thing on the very point of happening, mostly in narrative: “the soldiers were just about to scale the walls”.

phrases.english: What are you doing? What are you going to do?
I am going to recite a song I know

phrases.latin: quidnam futūrum est, sī creārit līberōs?
phrases.english: What is going to happen if he has children?

phrases.latin: crās tē vīctūrum, crās dīcis, Postume, semper
phrases.english: “Tomorrow I’m going to live,” you say, Postumus, always “tomorrow”

phrases.latin: in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē
phrases.english: we expect to come to Tusculum on the Nones or the day after

phrases.latin: factūrusne operae pretium sim … nec satis sciō
phrases.english: whether I am going to do something worth the effort, I don’t really know
